title: Results at noon
setting: Just before noon at the office. Last month Mai (Kimura-san at work) sat a bookkeeping exam, and the results go up online at twelve today. Her manager, Tanaka-san, stops by her desk to ask how she's feeling.

speakers.name: Tanaka-san
speakers.voice: male, 40s, calm and kind, polite office speech

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kimura-san, sengetsu, boki no shiken o ukemashita yo ne. kekka wa mou demashita ka?
lines.ja: 木村さん、先月、簿記の試験を受けましたよね。結果はもう出ましたか？
lines.kana: きむらさん、せんげつ、ぼきのしけんをうけましたよね。けっかはもうでましたか？
lines.english: Kimura-san, you took the bookkeeping exam last month, didn't you? Are the results out yet?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: mada desu. kyou no juuniji ni, kekka ga deru n desu.
lines.ja: まだです。今日の十二時に、結果が出るんです。
lines.kana: まだです。きょうのじゅうにじに、けっかがでるんです。
lines.english: Not yet. They come out today at twelve.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: mou sugu desu ne. jishin wa arimasu ka?
lines.ja: もうすぐですね。自信はありますか？
lines.kana: もうすぐですね。じしんはありますか？
lines.english: That's any minute now. Are you feeling confident?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: iie, zenzen. saigo no mondai ga, hotondo tokenakatta n desu.
lines.ja: いいえ、全然。最後の問題が、ほとんど解けなかったんです。
lines.kana: いいえ、ぜんぜん。さいごのもんだいが、ほとんどとけなかったんです。
lines.english: No, not at all. I barely got anywhere with the last question.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: daijoubu desu yo. ano shiken wa, nanajutten toreba ukarimasu kara.
lines.ja: 大丈夫ですよ。あの試験は、七十点取れば受かりますから。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶですよ。あのしけんは、ななじゅってんとればうかりますから。
lines.english: You'll be fine. On that exam, you pass if you get seventy.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: demo, nanajutten mo toretenai kamo shiremasen. shiken ni ochitara, dou shiyou.
lines.ja: でも、七十点も取れてないかもしれません。試験に落ちたら、どうしよう。
lines.kana: でも、ななじゅってんもとれてないかもしれません。しけんにおちたら、どうしよう。
lines.english: But I might not even have got seventy. What'll I do if I've failed?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: jitsu wa watashi mo, mukashi ano shiken ni nikai ochita n desu yo.
lines.ja: 実は私も、昔あの試験に二回落ちたんですよ。
lines.kana: じつはわたしも、むかしあのしけんににかいおちたんですよ。
lines.english: Actually, I failed that exam twice myself, years ago.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.kana: え、たなかさんがですか？

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: hai. shiken o sankai ukete, yatto ukatta n desu.
lines.ja: はい。試験を三回受けて、やっと受かったんです。
lines.kana: はい。しけんをさんかいうけて、やっとうかったんです。
lines.english: Yes. I took it three times before I finally passed.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sou na n desu ka. jaa, moshi shiken ni ochite mo, mata ukereba ii n desu ne.
lines.ja: そうなんですか。じゃあ、もし試験に落ちても、また受ければいいんですね。
lines.kana: そうなんですか。じゃあ、もししけんにおちても、またうければいいんですね。
lines.english: Really? So even if I fail, I can just take it again.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sou desu. hora, mou juuniji desu yo.
lines.ja: そうです。ほら、もう十二時ですよ。
lines.kana: そうです。ほら、もうじゅうにじですよ。

lines.speaker: mai
lines.ja: あ、結果出ました！七十二点取れました！
lines.kana: あ、けっかでました！ななじゅうにてんとれました！
lines.english: Oh, the results are up! I got seventy-two!

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: omedetou gozaimasu! ikkai de shiken ni ukatta n desu kara, sugoi desu yo.
lines.ja: おめでとうございます！一回で試験に受かったんですから、すごいですよ。
lines.kana: おめでとうございます！いっかいでしけんにうかったんですから、すごいですよ。
lines.english: Congratulations! You passed on your first try. That's impressive.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu! tanaka-san wa, ukatta toki, nanten totta n desu ka?
lines.ja: ありがとうございます！田中さんは、受かったとき、何点取ったんですか？
lines.kana: ありがとうございます！たなかさんは、うかったとき、なんてんとったんですか？
lines.english: Thank you! What did you get when you passed?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kyuujuuhachiten desu. onaji shiken o sankai mo ukereba, mondai mo oboechaimasu yo.
lines.ja: 九十八点です。同じ試験を三回も受ければ、問題も覚えちゃいますよ。
lines.kana: きゅうじゅうはちてんです。おなじしけんをさんかいもうければ、もんだいもおぼえちゃいますよ。
lines.english: Ninety-eight. Take the same exam three times and you end up knowing the questions.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, kyuujuuhachiten! jaa, rainen wa motto muzukashii shiken o ukete mimasu.
lines.ja: え、九十八点！じゃあ、来年はもっと難しい試験を受けてみます。
lines.kana: え、きゅうじゅうはちてん！じゃあ、らいねんはもっとむずかしいしけんをうけてみます。
lines.english: Ninety-eight! Then next year I'll try a harder exam.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: ii desu ne. moshi ochite mo, sankai made wa daijoubu desu yo.
lines.ja: いいですね。もし落ちても、三回までは大丈夫ですよ。
lines.kana: いいですね。もしおちても、さんかいまではだいじょうぶですよ。
lines.english: Good idea. And if you fail, you're fine up to three tries.

choices.english: Mai finds out she failed by two points, and Tanaka-san tells her she can just take it again.
Mai is sure she's failed, but when the results come out at twelve, she has passed on her first try.
Tanaka-san got ninety-eight on his first try, so he gives Mai tips before her exam.

questions.explanation: Lines 3-6: Mai has no confidence and fears she didn't get the seventy points she needs to pass. Line 12: the results come out and she got 72, and in line 13 Tanaka-san congratulates her on passing first time (ikkai de). A is wrong: 72 is two points over the pass mark, not under, and the 'just take it again' idea (line 10) comes before the results. C is wrong: Tanaka-san failed twice (line 7) and passed on his third try (line 9); the 98 was that third time (lines 14-15). Mai's exam was last month (line 1), so it's already over.

questions.english: At the start, how does Tanaka-san bring up the exam Mai sat last month?
questions.ja: 田中さんは、先月の試験のことを何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: たなかさんは、せんげつのしけんのことをなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: tanaka-san wa, sengetsu no shiken no koto o nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: You passed the bookkeeping exam last month, didn't you?
choices.romaji: sengetsu, boki no shiken ni ukarimashita yo ne.

choices.english: You 'took' the bookkeeping exam last month (toru, like English 'take'), didn't you?
choices.romaji: sengetsu, boki no shiken o torimashita yo ne.

choices.english: You took (sat) the bookkeeping exam last month, didn't you?
choices.romaji: sengetsu, boki no shiken o ukemashita yo ne.

questions.explanation: Line 1: 'boki no shiken o ukemashita yo ne'. You sit an exam with ukeru and o, and Tanaka-san says it again in line 9 (shiken o sankai ukete) and line 15 (onaji shiken o sankai mo ukereba). B follows English 'take', but toru goes with the score, not the exam: nanajutten toreba (line 5), nanajuuniten toremashita (line 12). A sounds very close, but ukaru (with ni) means pass, and at this point nobody knows the result yet. He asks whether the results are out in the same line, and Mai only finds out she passed in lines 12-13.

questions.english: Sora asks how your Japanese test went: "nihongo no shiken, nanten datta?" You got 85. Tell him your score.
questions.ja: 日本語の試験、何点だった？
questions.kana: にほんごのしけん、なんてんだった？
questions.answer: Give the number with ten fused on, then toru: hachijuugoten totta. Casual speech drops o. Don't use morau (that's a mark someone hands you), and never say shiken o totta: the exam is ukeru, the score is toru.

modelAnswers.romaji: hachijuugoten. kekkou ii ten toreta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 八十五点。けっこういい点取れたよ。
modelAnswers.english: Eighty-five. I managed a pretty good score.

questions.explanation: Score + toru is how Tanaka-san and Mai talk about marks: nanajutten toreba (line 5), nanajuuniten toremashita (line 12), nanten totta n desu ka (line 14). The toreta / toremashita form adds 'managed to get', as in Mai's line 12. hachijuugoten moratta would sound like a teacher just gave you the mark, and shiken o totta mixes up the exam (ukeru) with the score (toru). Sora asks casually, so answer casually.

questions.english: Mai tells Tanaka-san, "kyou no juuniji ni, kekka ga deru n desu." What happens at twelve?
questions.ja: 十二時に、何がありますか？
questions.kana: じゅうにじに、なにがありますか？
questions.romaji: juuniji ni, nani ga arimasu ka?

choices.english: She has to go out to collect her results.

questions.explanation: Line 2: kekka ga deru means the results come out, with the results as the subject, not Mai. At twelve (lines 11-12) she checks and says kekka demashita: they're up, and she got 72. B takes deru in its 'go out, leave' sense, but it's the results that come out, and Mai never leaves her desk. C is wrong because she sat the exam last month (line 1); only the results were still to come.

questions.english: Tanaka-san asks about an exam you took last month. You checked this morning: you passed. Tell him.
questions.ja: 先月の試験の結果は、もう出ましたか？
questions.kana: せんげつのしけんのけっかは、もうでましたか？
questions.romaji: sengetsu no shiken no kekka wa, mou demashita ka?
questions.answer: Say the results are out and you passed: shiken ni ukarimashita. The exam takes ni, and the verb is ukaru (ukarimashita), not ukeru (ukemashita), which would only say you sat it. goukaku shimashita also works.

modelAnswers.ja: はい、出ました。試験に受かりました！

modelAnswers.romaji: hai, kesa demashita. ikkai de shiken ni ukarimashita!
modelAnswers.ja: はい、今朝出ました。一回で試験に受かりました！
modelAnswers.english: Yes, they came out this morning. I passed on my first try!

questions.explanation: Tanaka-san says it this way in line 13 (ikkai de shiken ni ukatta) and line 9 (yatto ukatta). ukarimashita and ukemashita are one sound apart, and line 9 has both: shiken o sankai ukete, yatto ukatta (took it three times, finally passed). shiken o ukarimashita is wrong: the exam takes ni. Tanaka-san asks politely, so answer with -masu.

questions.english: You've just found out you failed an exam you took last month. Kenta sees you looking down and asks what's wrong. Tell him.
questions.ja: どうしたの？なんか元気ないね。
questions.kana: どうしたの？なんかげんきないね。
questions.romaji: dou shita no? nanka genki nai ne.
questions.answer: Say you failed with shiken ni ochiru, casually shiken ochichatta (-chatta adds 'sadly'). English 'fail' tempts shippai shita, but that means you messed something up; for a pass/fail result you 'fall': ochita.

modelAnswers.romaji: jitsu wa, shiken ochichatta n da.
modelAnswers.ja: 実は、試験落ちちゃったんだ。

modelAnswers.romaji: sengetsu no shiken, ochichatta. demo, mata ukeru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 先月の試験、落ちちゃった。でも、また受けるよ。
modelAnswers.english: I failed last month's exam. But I'll take it again.

questions.explanation: Mai and Tanaka-san use ochiru with ni for failing: shiken ni ochitara (line 6), ano shiken ni nikai ochita (line 7), shiken ni ochite mo (line 10). With a friend, ni usually drops and -chatta adds 'unfortunately'. shiken ni shippai shita means you blew it, which isn't the same as the result. Like Mai in line 10, you can add that you'll just take it again (mata ukeru), with ukeru, not ukaru.

newWords.english: times (counter): nikai twice, sankai three times; ikkai de on the first try
